title: Police officer in hospital after being shot in Nottingham
originalTitle: Police officer in hospital after being shot in Nottingham
content:
Assistant Chief Constable Claire Rukas, of Nottinghamshire Police, said: "This is a shocking incident and a sobering reminder of the potential dangers faced by officers as they work to protect and serve the public.

"As we investigate what happened and work to apprehend the individuals involved, my thoughts today are with the injured officer, his family and colleagues.

"I also ask that anyone with additional information shares this with us without delay. Even the smallest bit of information could make all the difference to this investigation."

BBC Reporter Viraj Soni, who is at the scene, has said that marked police cars are parked along the road, which is lined by fast food stores and shops.

Orange traffic cones have been laid out alongside items left on the road, he said.

The cordon has also been extended to St James's Street, where an officer is standing guard.

In a post on social media East Midlands Ambulance Service said sent its best wishes to the injured officer.

"Sending our heartfelt thoughts and support to the injured officer, his family, and all our colleagues at Nottinghamshire Police today," the post said.

"We're wishing him a full and speedy recovery."
